headline: Dynamics- and geometry-constrained models of noninvasive human brain activity
label: Constrained Neural Dynamics Modeling
summary: Noninvasive EEG and MEG modeling now incorporates neural dynamics and cortical geometry as explicit constraints, alongside systematic architecture evaluation.
synthesis: The four preprints model noninvasive human EEG and MEG recordings using explicit generative or predictive structure. An RNN framework with neural dynamic constraints models source-localized resting EEG from 114 participants and identifies parietal hubs across exogenous stimulus, task and spontaneous activity conditions. Geometric Basis Functions built from cortical-surface eigenmodes constrain EEG/MEG source imaging and improve whole-brain spatiotemporal reconstruction. A Conv-VaDE model with soft clustering yields interpretable EEG microstates, and an architecture grid search on LEMON resting-state data selects depth L=4. Integrative closed-loop dynamical models are proposed to pool recordings, behavior and anatomy for inferring principles of neural control. What is new is the combination of physically or anatomically grounded constraints, namely neural dynamics and cortical geometry, with systematic architecture evaluation.
